ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Article 109 of Law 2155 of 2021; Decree 1068 of 2015, Book 2, Chapter 3.4.1 (as amended); DIAN Resolution No. 000164 of 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB); Law 1121 of 2006; Law 526 of 1999; UIAF Circular Regulatoria Externa No. 009 of 2021; Criminal Code Articles 323, 324 and 345.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of foreign incorporation deed and certificate of good standing of the ultimate parent or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Registry or Companies House in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney granted to the Colombian incorporator or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary of the grantor's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with passport copies and proof of tax residence
Source of funds and source of wealth declaration supported by bank references
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank and licensed accountant in origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record certificate or police clearance for all directors and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National or federal police / judicial authority of the individual's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and legal representatives against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, Colombia's UIAF PEP Database, Interpol Red Notices, and Colombian Procuraduría and Contraloría lists. Due diligence must include ongoing transaction monitoring and enhanced measures for any politically exposed foreign or domestic person (FPP/PEP) detected; results must be retained for at least ten years per Colombian AML/CFT rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – www.rues.org.co with administrative processing via the local Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Spanish or any Romance or Latin-script language that is transliterated into Spanish legal characters for registration. The name must begin with a letter, consist exclusively of alphanumeric Latin characters, and the suffix 'S.A.S.' or 'SAS' must be included. Foreign language names must be accompanied by a notarized Spanish translation for the registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sociedad Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected by the Chamber of Commerce, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' with the same Chamber within ten (10) business days after notifying the rejection. If the name remains denied, a subsidiary 'recurso de apelación' may be submitted to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within five (5) business days of the sustentation hearing. The name may not be used commercially during the pendency of an appeal, and a new name reservation must be filed if the appeal is not accepted. The registration of an identical or confusingly similar name overrides any prior, inactive reservation after the 30-day window lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For the manufacture and export of medical diagnostic ultrasound consoles, a virtual office will not satisfy commercial substance requirements. The company must maintain and report a physical address in Colombia where the manufacturing operations, books and records, and regulatory files are located. The use of a registered agent or virtual office for the registered domicile alone is disallowed for this activity due to sectoral mandates of INVIMA and municipal zoning for industrial production.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (estimated >70% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first eighteen (18) months of operation by INVIMA, local health authorities, the DIAN, or the Superintendencia de Sociedades; manufacturing sites for Class II medical devices are subject to periodic Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) inspections).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUB (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) initial filing facilitation with DIAN

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Money-based legal fees per Colombian law market, inclusive of non-notarial services

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada, arts. 1-48) as incorporated with the Colombian Código de Comercio, especially arts. 110, 142, 158, and 161; complementary registration provisions in Decreto 1074 de 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social, acting through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) and the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución / Acta de Constitución, registered in the Cámara de Comercio and subsequently reflected in the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital under Ley 1258/2008. The S.A.S. may be formed with zero paid-in capital; subscribed capital may be paid in cash or in kind over the period set in the by-laws, without any mandatory escrow account rule under Colombian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION 1. The shareholders and incorporators hereby constitute the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada, adopt the by-laws, and approve the share subscriptions shown in the incorporation instrument. 2. The registered office is fixed at a place in Medellín, Colombia, subject to relocation by board decision. 3. The following officers are appointed: President and Legal Representative, Secretary, and Compliance Officer. 4. The Legal Representative is authorized to file the incorporation instrument before the Chamber of Commerce, obtain the NIT, open bank accounts, and complete municipal and sanitary licenses. 5. Any officer may execute all documents necessary to give legal effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Prevalidation and Activity Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES)/Ventanilla Única Empresarial
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the required name availability application through the RUES online platform, selecting ISIC 3250 as the principal economic activity. Pay the name search fee and obtain the certificate of name availability (certificado de homonimia) after verifying that the proposed corporate name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
required_dossiers: Completed RUES application form
Shareholder identification documents (cédula/foreign passport)
Power of attorney if the application is filed through a legal representative
Proposed primary and secondary ISIC activity codes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is refused, an alternative name may be submitted immediately through the same online platform; no additional corporate action is required before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Constitution Document and By-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private incorporators' meeting or, when required, a Colombian Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private constitution document (constitución privada) under Ley 1258/2008, containing the by-laws, share capital, board allocation, and legal representation rules. Each shareholder must sign the document or use an accepted electronic signature. If real property or other assets requiring public formality are contributed, the document must be executed before a Notary Public.
required_dossiers: Final by-laws text
Shareholders' identification and tax details
Name availability certificate
Detailed contribution schedule and forms of contribution
Acceptance letters of nominated statutory positions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or an incorporating shareholder identifies omissions, an accessory private agreement or amendment may be signed, and the corrected document supersedes the defective version before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Filing Before the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio principal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed constitution document and accompanying forms to the Cámara de Comercio of the domicile. Pay the mercantile registration fee and the promised contribution tax. The Chamber verifies the document, issues the mercantile registration record, and issues the initial Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal.
required_dossiers: Signed constitution document
Certificate of name availability
Completed RUES registration forms
Shareholder identification and address documentation
Payment receipt for registration fees
Legal representative acceptance and identity copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber returns observations, correct and re-submit the affected documents through RUES within the five-day curing period. Late registration may incur additional surcharges under Código de Comercio arts. 88 and 89 but may be cured by paying the applicable fine and filing a corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NIT and Tax Registry (RUT) Activation Before DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the registered certification of existence and the preliminary RUT generated by the RUES, finalize the Registro Único Tributario before DIAN, obtain the NIT, activate the 32-digit tax identification code, and set the electronic invoicing obligation as a manufacturer. The Legal Representative must validate identity through the DIAN virtual platform or by visiting the nearest DIAN office.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Legal representative government-issued identification
Proof of registered office address
Preliminary RUT from RUES
Bank data for tax refunds and electronic invoicing registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN portal rejects the electronic registration because of biometric or availability conflicts, schedule an in-person DIAN appointment to authenticate the Legal Representative's signature and correct the RUT before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Land Use, Building, and Fire Safety Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Municipal – Secretaría de Planeación, Curaduría Urbana, and Cuerpo de Bomberos
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal certificate of land use compatibility (certificado de uso de suelo) for an industrial/assembly operation under ISIC 3250. Apply for the building occupancy authorization or modification permit from the local Curaduría Urbana if the assembly plant requires construction changes. Secure the fire safety inspection and receive the Cuerpo de Bomberos certificate before starting operations.
required_dossiers: Property ownership or lease agreement
Architectural floor plan and assembly layout
Municipal land use certificate application
Fire prevention plan and installed suppression equipment
Civil liability insurance policy for the industrial site
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality denies land use because of incomplete technical drawings, re-file after correcting the square-meter calculations and usage percentages; an appeal may be submitted before the same administrative authority within ten days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: INVIMA Sanitary Registration and Good Manufacturing Practices Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos (INVIMA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the medical device sanitary registration application for the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console through the INVIMA technical platform. Under Decreto 4725 de 2005, provide the complete technical dossier proving conformity with applicable standards and the quality management system. Once approved, request the certificate of free sale and authorization to manufacture/export if distribution outside Colombia is intended.
required_dossiers: Technical dossier with device description, intended use, and clinical purpose
ISO 13485 quality management system certificate
Electrical safety and electromagnetic compatibility test reports (IEC 60601-series)
Software validation and cybersecurity declaration for ultrasound imaging console
Labeling and user manual in Spanish
Proof of payment for INVIMA sanitary registration tariff
Good Manufacturing Practices self-audit report and inspection checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INVIMA issues a requirement letter, the applicant may respond once within the legal term, usually ten working days, with supplementary technical evidence. If the registration is denied, the resources reposición and apelación may be exercised under the Código de Procedimiento Administrativo.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud y Protección Social / INVIMA (sanitary and medical-device regulation), with municipality-level physical planning authority for building and land-use compliance and regional Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) for environmental licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Dispositivo Médico for manufacturers of color Doppler ultrasound consoles, joined by Autorización de Funcionamiento del Establecimiento Fabricante and municipal Licencia de Funcionamiento Industrial.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and the applicable Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) competent for the state of Antioquia.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category of registration and environmental concept: full EIA not ordinarily required for the assembly of diagnostic ultrasound consoles; a Plan de Manejo Ambiental, a hazardous-waste generator registration, and emission/wastewater characterization are required for the industrial plant, subject to verification by the regional environmental authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliant industrial wastewater must conform with Decreto 1076 de 2015 and Resolución 0631 de 2015 for physicochemical discharges; VOC and particulate emissions must meet the stationary-source limits in Resolución 909 de 2008; hazardous electronic and biomedical waste must be disposed under Decreto 4741 de 2005 and Resolución 1362 de 2007 waste-generator registration rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos; structural load and seismic inspections by a registered architect or civil engineer for the assembly floor; occupational health and safety workplace clearance registered with the Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL); and emergency response plan validated by the local disaster risk management office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Unidad Administrativa Especial Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). Primary portals: www.dian.gov.co and MUISCA (muisca.dian.gov.co) for electronic registration, filing, invoicing clearance, and customs control.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent incorporating a Colombian S.A.S. must obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by filing the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) with DIAN. Procedure: (1) incorporate the S.A.S. before the Cámara de Comercio with a private document or notarized deed, appointing a legal representative domiciled in Colombia; (2) file the constitutional documents of the non-resident shareholder, apostilled and officially translated into Spanish; (3) register the RUT electronically via MUISCA or at a DIAN service point, attaching the certificate of existence and legal representation, the representative's Colombian identification, the corporate resolution appointing the representative, and a registered Colombian address; (4) DIAN validates the dossier and issues the NIT immediately; (5) update the RUT to reflect IVA-responsible status, exporter status, and any special customs regimes before the first export shipment. The NIT is a permanent alphanumeric identifier required for all invoicing, customs, banking, foreign-exchange, and tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the S.A.S. is a Colombian tax-resident separate taxpayer subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income; the standard CIT rate is 35% for tax year 2025; no pass-through or disregarded-entity election is available. Foreign-source income is included in the worldwide base with a foreign tax credit. Dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders carry an additional withholding: 10% for profits already taxed at entity level and 35% for profits not subject to entity-level taxation. Statutory CFC rules apply to foreign controlled entities. Export income remains taxable at the corporate level; the indirect-tax consequence of 0% IVA on exports is separate and does not remove income tax liability.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no check-the-box entity classification; the S.A.S. cannot be disregarded for tax purposes. Statutory elections and optional regimes include: (1) election of the SIMPLE aggregate regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación) for qualifying entities below the annual UVT turnover ceiling, which substitutes simplified presumptive components for ordinary CIT/IVA mechanics while preserving entity-level liability; (2) election to apply export VAT credits as a refund request, as an offset against other national taxes, or as a deductible cost when not recoverable; (3) application of the anti-hybrid and CFC rules introduced by Law 2277 of 2022, which are mandatory and do not allow taxpayer reclassification, although taxpayers must elect the factual classification of controlled arrangements and associated persons in annual informative returns; (4) election of statutory depreciation and investment-incentive methods for fixed assets; fiscal consolidation is not permitted for affiliated S.A.S. groups.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) — Colombian value added tax administered by DIAN, structured on the invoice-credit method with exclusions, exemptions, and a 0% export treatment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold: the S.A.S. becomes an IVA-responsible taxpayer from the first taxable sale, import, or export and must register via RUT. As an exception, natural persons with annual income up to 3,500 UVT (COP 164,727,500 for 2024, 1 UVT = COP 47,065) may qualify as 'no responsables'; corporate exporters and S.A.S. entities are always fully subject to IVA registration, declaration, and electronic invoicing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) under DIAN control. Invoices must be generated in UBL/XML format through an authorized technology provider or DIAN's free invoicing application, transmitted to DIAN's MUISCA web-service/API, pre-validated, and digitally signed; DIAN assigns the unique CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) stamp only after clearance approval. Documents transmitted after the transaction or without approved CUFE are void and cannot support VAT credits, deductions, or export refunds. All exporters must use the electronic export-invoice modality with QR code and match the invoice data to the DIAN customs export declaration within the statutory deadline.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% IVA (excluded from the taxable event, operating as zero-rating with input VAT credit rights) applies when goods physically depart from Colombian customs territory under DIAN customs supervision and are entered in the export declaration (DEX/DAM). For software and offshore services, zero-rating requires: (i) the service is provided to a non-resident beneficiary; (ii) the service is used exclusively outside Colombia; and (iii) the payment originates from a non-resident source (Decree 1625 of 2016, Article 1.3.1.4.9). The exporter must be IVA-responsible, hold the applicable INVIMA medical-device export authorization for the phased-array ultrasound console, and substantiate physical exit through transport and customs documents. Input VAT paid on production inputs and export logistics is recoverable through the export VAT refund procedure, subject to DIAN risk-based verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX/DAM) dispatched and accepted by DIAN
Bill of Lading (maritime) or Air Waybill (air cargo) evidencing physical departure from Colombian territory
Commercial invoice in DIAN electronic export-invoice modality with approved CUFE and QR code
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary or equivalent bank evidence of collection from the foreign buyer
Certificate of Origin (only when claiming tariff preference under an applicable FTA)
INVIMA export certificate and health registration for the medical device under ISIC 3250
Signed vendor's declaration of final destination, consignee, and end-user, executed by the legal representative
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN subjects exporters to risk-based audit and desk review of IVA refund claims, including cross-matching electronic invoices with customs DEX records and the foreign-exchange market reports. The exporter must retain the full documentation bundle for the statutory limitation period of generally five years. Clawback: improperly obtained refunds are fully reversed with default interest calculated on the lending rate basis plus surcharge, together with consumer-price-index adjustment. Penalties: (i) a sanction equal to 100% of the refund amount when the claim is inappropriate, rising up to 200% where supporting documents are falsified; (ii) criminal tax-fraud liability under Law 1819 of 2016 with imprisonment of 4 to 9 years where the evaded amount exceeds approximately 160,000 UVT; (iii) customs penalties under Law 1609 of 2013 for material misdeclarations in the export declaration; (iv) suspension or cancellation of RUT exporter status; and (v) retrospective reopening of prior export tax periods if the 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline is missed without valid authorization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), with the exchange-control regime applied through Authorized Foreign Exchange Intermediaries and supervised, for customs/exchange enforcement, by DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombian foreign exchange regulation is built on market-determined convertibility within a managed float. Current-account operations, including trade payments, service payments, and profit remittances, do not require prior central-bank approval and are convertible provided they are channeled through the authorized exchange market with a correct declaración de cambio. Capital-account transactions, including foreign equity contributions, are also permitted but must be routed through an authorized intermediary and registered with Banco de la República so that later dividend distributions, capital reductions, and repatriation can be justified. Profit remittance by the S.A.S. is not subject to FX rationing but requires payment of the applicable Colombian dividend withholding tax, confirmation that profits were declared and taxed in Colombia, and a clean exchange-control file evidencing inbound FDI registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The general statutory rule for goods exporters is canalización of export proceeds through a Colombian authorized foreign-exchange intermediary within 13 calendar months after the date of the export declaration/shipment; export of services carries a 6-month canalization calendar. There is no mandatory surrender ratio: Colombian law does not require a percentage of export FX to be converted into COP. The exporter must collect the proceeds through the regulated market, complete the corresponding export declaration of exchange (Formulario No. 2 remains the standard for goods), retain the DIAN export declaration (DEX) and supporting invoices/transport documents, and maintain the channeling records for at least five years. Untimely or omitted canalization exposes the S.A.S. to fines and administrative sanctions under the Colombian foreign-exchange regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low-to-Medium for a regulated exporting S.A.S. Offshore fintech EMIs are not licensed by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia and cannot satisfy the statutory canalización requirement for export proceeds; an offshore EMI cannot issue Colombian Formulario No. 2 change declarations. The only compliant use is as a secondary collections tool if a distributor/payer remits there, provided the balance is promptly swept by SWIFT MT103 into the entity's Colombian bank account, where the exchange declaration is made. Maintaining export collections exclusively outside the Colombian authorized market creates foreign-exchange-control, transfer-pricing, and taxable-presence risks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Colombian commercial banks generally require an in-person or recorded interactive KYC interview with the legal representative, principal shareholders, and beneficial owners at initial onboarding. Fully remote opening for a newly formed foreign-owned S.A.S. is not guaranteed; in practice, the directors must appoint a Colombian resident legal representative by notarized public power of attorney (poder general) to appear before the bank, execute account documents, and answer KYC questions. Passport pages, local NIT/RUT, Articles of Incorporation, board resolutions, and UBO/sworn-source-of-funds forms are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner without Colombian credit history or local financial footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of the parent/beneficial owner; certified S.A.S. bylaws and current NIT/RUT; UBO schema showing full ownership chain; source-of-wealth files; bank reference from the home-country bank; audited or management financial statements; board resolution authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical-imaging exporter expected to receive third-party payments from hospital distributors rather than named end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed distribution/manufacturing representation contracts; INVIMA sanitary registration or hazard-free medical-equipment classification letter; sales invoices and quantity-price reconciliation; Incoterms and export transport documents; explanation of payment routing; distributor counterparty KYC information.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly created S.A.S. perceived as a shell or nominee structure with no operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Physical office lease in Colombia; local payroll and social-security records; equipment and inventory photos/invoices; ISO 13485/quality certificates; product purchase orders and pipeline; audited/pro-forma revenue projections; company website and business emails linked to Colombian operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de Matrícula Mercantil (annual renewal of the commercial registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local Cámara de Comercio where the S.A.S. maintains its registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a surcharge equal to 10% of the applicable registration tariff and renders the registration inactive; prolonged non-renewal under chamber rules exposes the company to administrative strike-off and loss of the legal existence certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Estados Financieros (deposit of fiscal-year financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio; concurrently available to Superintendencia de Sociedades for supervised subjects
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of the following fiscal year and within the annual renewal window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely failure to file may result in fines imposed by the Superintendencia de Sociedades and the Chamber, including exclusion from renewal and penalties for misstatements in the annual registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Reporte Anual de Beneficiarios Finales (annual ultimate beneficial owner report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 1 July of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, late filing, or incomplete information is subject to monetary penalties under Article 651 of the Colombian Tax Code; repeat noncompliance may block the issuance of administrative certificates and tax clearance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Colombian S.A.S. must appoint a statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) and have independent audited financial statements if, as of the immediately preceding year-end, gross assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approximately COP 8.1 billion), gross revenues exceed 3,000 SMMLV (approximately COP 4.9 billion), or the company has more than 30 shareholders; entities not meeting these thresholds and not publicly accountable are exempt from statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under the technical framework issued through Decree 2420 of 2015: full IFRS for Group 1 public-accountability entities, IFRS for SMEs for Group 2, and micro-entity IFRS for Group 3; this exporter should apply Group 2 IFRS for SMEs unless its size, legal listing, or public-accountability status places it in Group 1.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must file the annual beneficial-owner report with DIAN by 1 July based on the year-end shareholding structure and must update the share register contemporaneously with every transfer. Each transfer that moves a natural person above the 5% ownership or control threshold, or changes the ultimate beneficial owner, must be reflected in the DIAN report in the next annual confirmation; non-reporting is treated as omission before the tax administration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share Transfer Book and Pledge Record

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150–500 per year depending on city and chamber tariffs
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000–8,000 depending on revenue and asset complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Colombian corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta) applies at a flat 35% for tax year 2023 onwards. Manufacturing companies may claim the standard deductions for payroll, raw materials, depreciation, financial costs and R&D. Qualifying science, technology and innovation investments can obtain a 150% to 175% deduction, while certain capital-intensive industrial fixed-asset investments may be entitled to accelerated depreciation or a percentage-based tax credit subject to DIAN authorization. No broad patent box for medical imaging is available; the effective rate for an exported medical-device manufacturer is generally the full 35% unless specific investment incentives are certified.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 (Sociedades y Asimiladas) is the official annual corporate income tax return and net wealth tax declaration, filed electronically through DIAN's Mutual (invited electronic filing) or Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales online portal (Airus/Información Electrónica). The return is accompanied by supporting annexes such as the transfer pricing sworn declaration (Anexo PI) where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return must be filed by the fiscal year-end deadline established by DIAN, generally no later than the end of the second or third month after the fiscal year end for calendar-year taxpayers. Actual due dates are staggered according to the last digit of the company's NIT, with releases beginning in late March. For a Colombian SAS with a 31 December fiscal year, Form 110 is typically due between early April and late April for ordinary taxpayers and one month earlier for large taxpayers, as published annually by DIAN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 62 - Total tax payable or balance in favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of income tax, over the tax prepaid separately, after subtracting withholdings on account, tax withholdings on the company's income, and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend remittances must be reported separately; any withholding tax on dividends is withheld and declared in Form 110 or the relevant monthly withholding form and cannot be offset against the corporate tax payable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 110 subjects the taxpayer to a penalty of 5% of the tax not paid on time for each full or partial month of delay, up to a maximum of 100% of the unpaid tax, plus current interest. Late filing without tax due incurs a sanction equal to 0.5% of gross income, capped at the greater of 1,500 UVT or the amount otherwise taxed, calculated by DIAN. Additional penalties of 1% of the tax assessed per month apply for errors in taxable income declarations or for non-taxed balance in favor, with potential criminal exposure for intentionally omitting facts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory dividend withholding tax for non-resident shareholders is 5% on the portion of dividends paid out of profits already subject to Colombian corporate income tax. For dividends distributed from profits that were exempt or not taxed at the corporate level (e.g., certain statutory exemptions), the withholding rate is 35%; an additional surcharge of 4% may apply to individual beneficiaries for the portion of untaxed profits, bringing the total to 39%. For a Colombian SAS manufacturing medical devices, ordinary dividends from taxed engineering revenue are taxed at 5%. If the foreign shareholder is a resident of a jurisdiction with an effective double tax treaty, the 5% treaty rate may be reduced to 0% only where the treaty expressly eliminates the withholding tax and the distribution is not considered a hidden profit distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax treaty (DTA) in Colombia, the shareholder must: (i) obtain a current Certificate of Tax Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the competent tax authority of the destination jurisdiction; (ii) complete the DIAN authorization form or sworn declaration of beneficial ownership (Formulario 150/DIAN 'Solicitud de Trato Exento'); (iii) provide the certificate of residence and a legalized power of attorney where requested to the payer before the remittance is made; (iv) prove the beneficiary is the actual owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty through the transactional documents; and (v) retain the supporting documentation for the five-year statute of limitations. Colombia's active DTAs generally follow the OECD Model, but relief is not automatic and the certificate must be submitted to the DIAN customs/withholding agent before the payment or no later than the deadline for the relevant declaration, otherwise the statutory withholding must be applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents for the use or exploitation of software, patents, trademarks, industrial know-how, and technical assistance are subject to a statutory withholding tax of 33% under domestic law; this rate is commonly reduced to 10% or zero under the bilateral tax treaties, and the 15% rate applies to technical services qualifying as knowledge transmission. Interest on external credit loans registered at the Banco de la República is generally subject to a 15% domestic withholding rate, reduced to 10% under most Colombian DTAs; non-registered related-party loans attract a 20% withholding rate plus transfer-pricing consequences. For royalties or interest to a related party, the ABR (Beneficial Ownership) requirement must be met and a transfer-pricing analysis prepared.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Colombian transfer pricing obligations are framed in UVT (Unidad de Valor Tributario). For tax year 2024, one UVT equals COP 47,324. A Local File is mandatory when the aggregate value of controlled transactions with related parties in the prior fiscal year equals or exceeds 100,000 UVT (approximately COP 4,732,400,000). A Master File is mandatory when the consolidated transactions with related parties equal or exceed 1,000,000 UVT (approximately COP 47,324,000,000) or when the multinational group has consolidated revenue above the DIAN threshold. A taxpayer below these UVT amounts but classified as a large contributor, or whose transactions exceeded 100,000 UVT in any previous year, may still be required to file the sworn transfer-pricing information return (Form 120) and maintain contemporaneous documentation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Plus OECD-sanctioned residual methods with DIAN acceptance on evidence
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia imposes no standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) as seen in UAE or Cayman, but applies an anti-abuse doctrine through the OECD 'beneficial ownership' concept, Article 260-2 E.T. transfer-pricing rules, and DIAN general anti-avoidance principles. A Colombian SAS that merely invoices foreign transactions from a mailbox or virtual office, without real management, employees, warehouse or operation for the color Doppler ultrasound device production, is subject to recharacterization as a shell company, denial of treaty relief, and liability for evasion. The company must maintain physical assets, qualified personnel, payroll and records in Colombia to reflect genuine manufacturing activities. The concept of 'economic substance' is assessed by examining whether the tested functions performed in Colombia are equivalent to the risks assumed and remuneration earned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting export revenues, over-invoicing costs in foreign related parties, inflating royalty deductions, artificial shifting of Colombian manufacturing margin to a tax-haven intermediary, or backdating invoices for color Doppler ultrasound consoles. Also, failing to present the TP Local File when thresholds are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN will adjust income and impose a penalty equal to 100% of the omitted tax plus inflation-adjusted interest, with additional penalties of 1% to 5% of the tax assessed for inaccurate returns. In aggravated cases, a non-deductible penalty up to 30% of the improvised value and administrative closure of the operation may apply. Moreover, the tax deficiency cannot be offset by subsequent profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and directors of the Colombian SAS may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporation tax when they knowingly participate in the smuggling, rendering false invoices, or signing declarations that hide taxable facts (Arts. 794 and 2158 C.C.; Article 27-3 of Law 224/1995). The DIAN may enforce collection against directors' personal assets, impose travel bans, restrict residence, and criminal prosecution under Colombian Criminal Code Art. 434A (tax evasion) can lead to imprisonment of 4 to 9 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Colombian entity with no production capacity, no industrial facility, or no medical-device inventory; using an address-only representation; delegating all operational functions to related foreign entities; and not demonstrating managerial decisions made in Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the corporate entity for tax purposes, reallocate the entire taxable income to the foreign principal, refuse dividend-remittance treaty relief, and eliminate all deductions. It can also cancel the RUT and impose a desertion penalty of 0.5% of gross income on the entity. Any improper repayment of taxes or foreign tax credits is recaptured with interest at the official rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is penetrable where the company acts as a mere conduit or instrumentality; shareholders and directors can be held personally liable in the amount of the unpaid corporate tax, and foreign directors can be barred from re-entering Colombia for serious tax fraud. Criminal ly, directors who intentionally operate a sham entity may be tried for documentary fraud and illicit use of legal status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing medical-device payments through shell accounts, issuing false commercial invoices for export transactions, under-invoicing freight/insurance through related parties, or receiving reimbursement in cryptocurrencies from high-risk jurisdictions without a registered cross-border trade agreement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Colombia's Financial Analysis Unit (UIAF) and DIAN can freeze bank accounts, seize funds equal to the transaction value, and impose fines equal to 100% to 500% of the laundered value. The exporter may also be blacklisted from Swift LC/TT wire operations and lose its export license, in addition to criminal fines of 12,000 to 30,000 minimum wages. The Ministry of Health suspension of the manufacturer's sanitary registration for breach of customs/pharmaceutical controls may constitute an administrative closure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners engaging in money-laundering, falsifying or using counterfeit trade documents, or participating in fraudulent cross-border wire transfers are subject to confiscation of assets, travel bans, and imprisonment of 10 to 16 years under Colombian Law 599/2000, Art. 323. Compliance programs and adequate documentation are required to prevent personal criminal accountability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold the 5% or 35% dividend tax on remittance to non-resident shareholders, or alternatively paying dividends out of profits that have not been properly credited with the foreign parent's share of tax, while also failing to remit the withheld tax to DIAN within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent (the Colombian SAS) is personally liable to DIAN for the tax withheld, plus a sanction of 5% of the unpaid withhold per month of delay capped at 100%, and an error penalty of 1% of the payment when the amount is under-withheld. The non-resident shareholder can also be assessed the tax personally with surcharge interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative who signs the Form 110 or the withholding declaration and authorizes dividend payments without withholding may be personally liable for the uncollected tax. Criminal penalties apply if money is extracted through fake dividends, and the DIAN may impose a personal guarantee or prohibition on the director from leaving Colombia while the collection case is pending.
